boyle_robert: The given name of the author Robert Boyle.
boyle_carneades: The sceptical speaker in Boyle’s dialogue. Named for the ancient philosopher.
boyle_philoponus: Boyle’s spokesman for the chymical position.
boyle_helmont: Jan Baptist van Helmont, experimenter cited by Boyle.
boyle_initial_g: Initial as cited in Boyle’s marginal note. The witness does not expand the name.
boyle_initial_f: Initial as cited in Boyle’s marginal note. The witness does not expand the name.
boyle_initial_h: Initial as cited in Boyle’s marginal note. The witness does not expand the name.
boyle_leucippus: The absent atomist whom the speakers hoped would attend. Distinct from the ancient historical namesake.
boyle_organum: The cited logical works of Aristotle.
boyle_initial_j: Initial used by the bookseller in the supplied imprint.
boyle_crooke: The bookseller J. Crooke, whose address is given at the sign of the Ship.
boyle_claveus: Gasto Claveus, lawyer and author of the report on gold and silver.
boyle_gasto: The personal name of Gasto Claveus in the supplied text.
boyle_agricola: Georgius Agricola, quoted on furnace deposits.
boyle_osteocolla: The apothecaries’ name for the material called bone stone in the text.
boyle_pompholix: Historical Greek name for the light furnace sublimate; in this quotation the name itself is under discussion.
boyle_spodos: The Greek word for ash, applied to the heavier furnace deposit.
boyle_pyrites: Historic name covering several spark-producing stones; here the name of the Ancients as quoted.
boyle_gunther: The author cited for the account of sulphur in the earth.
boyle_alkahest: The named universal solvent reported by Helmont; the narrator distinguishes the report from his own testimony.
boyle_archidoxis: Archidoxis, the work of Paracelsus from whose sixth book the Latin passage is quoted.
boyle_hermes: Hermes in the alchemical expression seal of Hermes; distinct from the biblical personal name.
boyle_nova_zembla: The island region named in the Arctic wintering account.
boyle_november: The named November of the wintering account.
boyle_october: The named October of the wintering account.
boyle_gerard_de_veer: Gerard de Veer as named in Boyle’s copy of the expedition report.
boyle_john_cornelyson: John Cornelyson as named in Boyle’s copy of the expedition report.
boyle_amsterdam: European port from which the expedition sailed.
boyle_may: Calendar month named in the late-sown garden trial.
boyle_diogenes_laertius: Historian of Greek philosophers cited on Thales.
boyle_thales: The ancient Greek thinker associated here with water as the principle of things.
boyle_justin_martyr: Justin Martyr cited for the antiquity of the view.
boyle_apollonius: Apollonius whose Argonautica has the scholium discussed here.
boyle_argonautica: The poem about the Argonauts, cited by book.
boyle_athenagoras: The writer named beside the citation of Orpheus.
boyle_plutarch: Ancient Greek author cited on the testimony of Homer.
boyle_strabo: The geographer cited for ancient accounts of Indian beliefs.
boyle_democritus: Ancient atomist identified as a pupil of Leucippus.
boyle_leucippus_historic: The ancient philosopher. Separate semantic identity from the absent participant in Boyle’s dialogue.
boyle_moschus: Phoenician thinker to whom some writers ascribed the atomical hypothesis.
boyle_rochas: The French chymist whose reported experiment Carneades recounts.
boyle_merachephet: The Hebrew word discussed by the speaker; preserves the supplied form as an object of linguistic discussion.
boyle_balsam_samech: The alchemical preparation named in the passage; a historical medicine, retaining the authorial attribution.
boyle_laurembergius: Author of the notes cited on a tasteless menstruum.
boyle_sala: Author of the aphorisms on which Laurembergius comments.
boyle_elaterium: Historical name for the purgative preparation Hippocrates is cited as mentioning.
boyle_sennertus: Daniel Sennert, cited here in support of a chemical theory of mixture.
boyle_crama: Greek term for a blended drink, used here for wine diluted with water.
boyle_synchysis: The Greek term for confusion or fusion in the Stoic account of blending.
boyle_roger_bacon: The English writer named by Eleutherius.
boyle_quercetanus: The Latin name under which Joseph Du Chesne is cited.
boyle_billich: The writer through whom the diamond passage is cited.
boyle_thessalus: Title name in the cited Thessalus redivivus.
boyle_lignum_nephriticum: The historical wood whose infusion is described as blue in the colour experiment.
boyle_lully: The name under which the cited alchemical works circulated.
boyle_gas: Helmont’s coined name, quoted here as an example of a word the practitioners could choose.
boyle_blas: Helmont’s coined technical name for an agency of motion, cited beside Gas as a term of art.
boyle_beguinus: Jean Béguin, author quoted concerning the distillation of sugar of lead.
boyle_alexander_van_suchten: Chymical author cited on a green mercury of copper.
boyle_barthias: Commentator on Béguin, cited here by Boyle.
boyle_platerus: Physician cited concerning medicines in their natural state.
boyle_jer: Abbreviated citation of the commentator, as printed.
boyle_baptista_porta: Giambattista della Porta, named in the discussion of luminous distillates.
boyle_caves_goutieres: Named source, locality, or historical designation in the accounts of mineral growth.
boyle_van_linschoten: Named source, locality, or historical designation in the accounts of mineral growth.
boyle_fallopius: Named source, locality, or historical designation in the accounts of mineral growth.
boyle_pliny: Named source, locality, or historical designation in the accounts of mineral growth.
boyle_elba: Named source, locality, or historical designation in the accounts of mineral growth.
boyle_cesalpinus: Named source, locality, or historical designation in the accounts of mineral growth.
boyle_tyrrhenian: Named source, locality, or historical designation in the accounts of mineral growth.
boyle_saga: Named source, locality, or historical designation in the accounts of mineral growth.
boyle_lygii: Named source, locality, or historical designation in the accounts of mineral growth.
boyle_boccaccio: Named source, locality, or historical designation in the accounts of mineral growth.
boyle_certaldo: Named source, locality, or historical designation in the accounts of mineral growth.
boyle_fiesole: Named source, locality, or historical designation in the accounts of mineral growth.
boyle_etruria: Named source, locality, or historical designation in the accounts of mineral growth.
boyle_amberg: Named source, locality, or historical designation in the accounts of mineral growth.
boyle_asyllum: Named source, locality, or historical designation in the accounts of mineral growth.
boyle_gerhardus: Named source, locality, or historical designation in the accounts of mineral growth.
boyle_joachim: Named source, locality, or historical designation in the accounts of mineral growth.
boyle_schreterus: Named source, locality, or historical designation in the accounts of mineral growth.
boyle_annaberg: Named source, locality, or historical designation in the accounts of mineral growth.
boyle_valehius: Named source, locality, or historical designation in the accounts of mineral growth.
boyle_strasburg: Named source, locality, or historical designation in the accounts of mineral growth.
boyle_mariakirch: Named source, locality, or historical designation in the accounts of mineral growth.
boyle_johannes_agricola: Named source, locality, or historical designation in the accounts of mineral growth.
boyle_poppius: Named source, locality, or historical designation in the accounts of mineral growth.
boyle_schwadt: Named source, locality, or historical designation in the accounts of mineral growth.
boyle_johannes_name: Forename of the traveller and chymist Agricola, distinguished here from Georgius.
boyle_georgius_name: Forename explicitly distinguished from Johannes in the source.
boyle_acosta: José de Acosta, eyewitness quoted on native gold and silver in the Americas.
boyle_papas: Reported local name for the rounded pieces of native silver, retained as a quoted term.
boyle_rondelet: Guillaume Rondelet, the writer on fishes cited by Boyle.

boyle_chymistry: The early modern practice of examining and transforming materials by trials and operations, including medical and alchemical work.
boyle_chymist: A practitioner of chymical operations. This designation alone implies neither gold making nor assent to the three principles.
boyle_spagyrist: A practitioner of the art defined by separation and reunion, especially in the Paracelsian tradition.
boyle_alchymist: An early modern practitioner of the art of transforming substances. In the title the general body of alchymists is meant.
boyle_principle: A proposed primary material constituent of other bodies; its status is at issue in the dialogue.
boyle_hypostatic: Predicated of a proposed principle held to subsist as a real substance in its own right.
boyle_paradox: A proposition running counter to received opinion, whether or not internally contradictory.
boyle_skeptic: Weighing reasons while withholding assent. In this work a questioning stance rather than a claim that nothing can be known.
boyle_material_body: A physically constituted body or sample, whether living or inanimate.
boyle_mixt: A body understood as constituted from diverse ingredients. No modern mixture–compound distinction is assumed.
boyle_peripatetic: A follower of the Aristotelian school of natural philosophy.
boyle_salt_principle: The saline principle of the spagyric triad. Distinguished from common salt and particular salts.
boyle_sulphur_principle: The putative sulphurous principle, often associated with combustibility or oil.
boyle_mercury_principle: The putative mercurial principle, often associated with volatility. Distinct from metallic quicksilver.
boyle_particle: A small portion of matter; implies no indivisibility or modern atomic theory.
boyle_laboratory: A workroom equipped for chemical trials, prominently those involving furnaces.
boyle_phenomenon: Something observable in nature whose underlying cause remains to be explained.
boyle_protocol: An instruction specifying what is to be done, distinguished from testimony of work actually performed.
boyle_testimony: A report grounded in a witness’s own experience of the trial.
boyle_theory: An organized account of causes; a system to be examined rather than the work of operating a furnace.
boyle_operation: An actual manipulation performed as part of a craft.
boyle_adept: An acknowledged master of the chymical art, distinguished from both a deceiver and a mere operator.
boyle_laborant: A hands-on laboratory worker, here distinguished from one who also understands the principles.
boyle_texture: The arrangement of small parts in a body, irrespective of how the surface feels.
boyle_fixed: Remaining under heating in the operative sense, contrasted with material carried away as vapour.
boyle_volatile: Readily carried away on heating; applied to material rather than temperament.
boyle_objection: A stated reason against a proposition.
boyle_preamble: Words setting out the case before an argument or conversation.
boyle_invitation: An express request that another person undertake something.
boyle_accident: An attribute or event affecting a body, distinguished from what constitutes it.
boyle_qualm: Hesitation arising from a particular doubt or concern.
boyle_challenge: To contest a thesis or argument in debate.
boyle_adversary: The party arguing an opposing case.
boyle_deny: The negative side of a disputed universal proposition.
boyle_measure: The degree of exactness in the statement of an argument or result.
boyle_experience: Knowledge founded in familiarity with the work itself.
boyle_bias: A judgment already formed that colours the reading of evidence.
boyle_specimen: An example presented for examination; in the preface an illustrative piece of writing.
boyle_commonwealth_letters: The community engaged in learning and exchanging knowledge.
boyle_hermetic: Of the alchemical tradition associated with Hermes; here, its body of doctrine.
boyle_atom: A material unit held by atomists to be indivisible; denotes the ancient claim.
boyle_shorthand: Abbreviated writing used to record spoken exchanges.
boyle_solitude: The privacy of a person apart from company.
boyle_analysis: A trial in which a material is divided to investigate its constituents. Whether the resulting materials were present beforehand is disputed.
boyle_elixir: The sought alchemical agent of transmutation.
boyle_empiric: An experiential practitioner, here Themistius’s dismissive term for a chymist.
boyle_apriori: Reasoning from a prior cause to its effects.
boyle_aposteriori: Reasoning from observed effects to a cause.
boyle_litharge: The oxidized lead produced in cupellation, also called litharge of gold in the example. The name does not designate gold.
boyle_cupel: A porous assay vessel used in the refining example.
boyle_calcine: To reduce a material to a calx by the action of heat.
boyle_phlegm: The watery fraction obtained on distillation in the five-product enumeration. Distinct from the bodily humour.
boyle_spirit_distilled: The volatile fraction yielded on distilling, distinguished from phlegm in Carneades’s list.
boyle_refiner: A worker who purifies a metal as in the example with gold and lead.
boyle_talc: The mineral referred to as Talck, whose Venetian calcined form is used as an example.
boyle_pasteboard: Stiff material formed from layers of paper, used for the astronomer’s teaching sphere.
boyle_system: An organized whole of interrelated opinions or explanations.
boyle_proposition: A statement set out separately for examination and assent.
boyle_microscope: An optical instrument for viewing objects too small to distinguish clearly with the unaided eye.
boyle_corpuscle: A small constituent body proposed to persist through changes of composition. Unlike an atom it can itself be composite.
boyle_cluster: A group of minute material parts considered together as a persistent unit.
boyle_void: Empty space in the atomists’ physical account, not privation in a moral sense.
boyle_antimony: The mineral material Boyle calls antimony, kept distinct from its separated metallic regulus.
boyle_regulus: The separated metallic portion of a mineral preparation.
boyle_martial_regulus: Boyle’s martial regulus, a chymical preparation associated with iron; the historical designation is retained.
boyle_aqua_regia: Royal water, the solvent named for its action on gold.
boyle_aqua_fortis: Strong water, the historical acid liquid so called.
boyle_menstruum: A dissolving medium or solvent; no biological sense is implied.
boyle_sublime: To cause material to rise in a vessel and collect again above.
boyle_amalgam: A mixture or union of metallic mercury with another metal; narrower than a mixture in general.
boyle_precipitate: Material separated from a liquid as a solid powder.
boyle_vitriol: The family of substances historically called vitriols, here in the term oil of vitriol.
boyle_cinnabar: The red mercurial substance Boyle describes as formed with sulphur.
boyle_malleable: Able to take shape under the hammer.
boyle_saline: Possessing a salt-like character; applied to substances of several kinds.
boyle_cap_paper: The paper named in Boyle’s filtration of a liquor.
boyle_distil: To separate a liquid fraction by vaporization and collection of the condensed drops.
boyle_substantial_form: The scholastic explanatory form held to make a thing the kind of substance it is. Distinguished from geometrical shape.
boyle_dissolve: To pass into or disperse through a solvent; distinct from fusion by heat.
boyle_concession: A proposition allowed for the purposes of the argument.
boyle_temperament: The balance of the primary qualities ascribed to the mixture of the four elements.
boyle_variety: Multiplicity of different kinds, as distinct from sheer number.
boyle_retort: A distilling vessel with a bent neck.
boyle_caput: Caput mortuum, the material left after distillation; the name does not establish that it is elementary earth.
boyle_balneum: A bath used to apply gentle heat to a vessel.
boyle_rectify: To redistil a collected fraction; distinguished from the first distillation.
boyle_vitrify: To convert a material into glass.
boyle_homogeneous: Of a single kind in the respect under discussion.
boyle_heterogeneous: Differing in material kind, not merely differing in particle size.
boyle_camphor: The fragrant volatile material Boyle calls camphire; distinguished from amber.
boyle_guaiacum: The medicinal hardwood named guajacum by Boyle.
boyle_pestle: The implement used to break material into finer portions.
boyle_flowers: Fine deposited solids called flowers, not parts of a plant.
boyle_alloy: Metal mixed with another metal, here the base material in silver.
boyle_crucible: A refractory vessel for maintaining a melt. Distinct from the porous assay cupel and the necked distilling retort.
boyle_condense: To gather from a vapour or fume into denser material. The product can be liquid or solid.
boyle_heat_degree: An intensity of applied heat, not necessarily a numeric scale.
boyle_sublimation: The operation of depositing volatilized material above its original position.
boyle_distillation: The operation by which a liquid fraction is raised and collected.
boyle_analysis_agent: Something by which a composite is resolved into products.
boyle_geometry: Inquiry into shape and measure in the reference to geometrically formed crystals.
boyle_granule: A little grain of material, such as silver in the pores of a used crucible; neither cereal nor a unit of weight.
boyle_pore: A minute opening in a body such as the wall of a crucible.
boyle_calx: Powdery product left by calcination of a solid; in this passage a lead-bearing furnace product.
boyle_cadmia: Historical furnace material named cadmia in Agricola’s account; no claim of a single modern chemical composition.
boyle_bonestone: The historical lapis ossifragus, also called osteocolla here.
boyle_muscovy_glass: The material known as Muscovy glass, the clear sheeted mineral, distinct from manufactured glass.
boyle_boxwood: Wood of the box tree used in the distillation trial.
boyle_sal_ammoniac: The historical salt which Boyle describes as subliming and which he analyses in terms of common and urinous salts.
boyle_urinous_salt: Historical category of volatile salt identified by its sharp urinous odour; not limited to salts extracted from urine.
boyle_acid: Possessing the sharp or sour quality by which Boyle recognizes an acid liquor.
boyle_digest: To keep materials in sustained contact, usually with gentle warmth, over time; distinct from digestion of food.
boyle_digestion: Prolonged contact of the materials, often with gentle heat.
boyle_alkali: The historical category of alcalizate salts, including those from plant ashes.
boyle_tartar: The solid deposit from wine. Distinct from a Tartar person and from Tartarus.
boyle_oil_vitriol: Boyle’s oil of vitriol; an acid liquor of vitriol, not an oil from a plant or animal.
boyle_spirit_nitre: Historical spirit of nitre obtained from saltpetre. Distinguishes this reagent from the biblical cleansing mineral.
boyle_receiver: The vessel attached for collecting products passing out of the retort.
boyle_quicklime: The unslaked burnt lime of the historical laboratory.
boyle_ignite: To take fire or to set alight, as specified by subject and voice.
boyle_attachment: Clay or sealing compound used at vessel joints.
boyle_solution: A substance dissolved in a liquid, or the resulting liquor, as opposed to molten metal.
boyle_sublimate_product: The historical sublimate made from salts and quicksilver. Distinct from the general process of subliming.
boyle_mass: An aggregate, lump, or body of material, as distinct from weight as a measured quantity.
boyle_sulphur_material: An observed substance resembling common brimstone. Its identity and simplicity may be under dispute; the term does not commit the speaker to the alchemists’ Sulphur principle.
boyle_marcasite: Early modern group of sparkling or brassy mineral substances. The historical term is broader than modern mineralogical marcasite.
boyle_fixedness: Degree to which a substance remains under applied heat.
boyle_volatility: Relative readiness of matter to rise and pass over in an operation; may depend on the degree of heat.
boyle_colcothar: The residual material from heated vitriol named in Boyle’s experiment.
boyle_merc_dulcis: Mercurius dulcis, the historical preparation called sweet mercury.
boyle_pelican: The circulating vessel named for the pelican in the alchemical account.
boyle_magistery: Paracelsus’s technical name for the preparation obtained at the end of his process.
boyle_continuity: The material continuity of parts which are not separated from one another.
boyle_dulcify: To sweeten or render milder in the historical laboratory sense; includes removal of salts by washing where the context supplies it.
boyle_arctic_circle: Northern polar circle used as a geographical reference in the historical account.
boyle_squash: The quick-growing Indian squash planted in the weighing trial, related to the pumpion; distinct from the Shakespearean immature pea pod.
boyle_gardener: The garden worker who planted, weighed and reported his measurements. No personal name is supplied.
boyle_spearmint: The particular mint propagated from a cutting in springwater.
boyle_lemon_balm: The aromatic herb called balme in the water trial, distinct from a healing ointment.
boyle_pennyroyal: The aromatic herb named separately from spearmint and balm in the plant trial.
boyle_empyreumatic: Having the characteristic burnt smell caused by strong heating, as in a distilled fraction.
boyle_foot_length: Historical unit of length, distinguished from a person’s foot by its use with a measure.
boyle_water_plant: Supply water to the soil or plant in a growing trial.
boyle_cohobation: Repeated redistillation in which the distillate is returned to the material it was distilled from.
boyle_chalk: The soft white mineral material used in the account.
boyle_moss: The low-growing moss named among the possible growths in standing water.
boyle_mathematics: Study of number and measure; distinguishes the correspondent’s profession from the physician’s.
boyle_mistion: Formation of a mixed body. This disputed term leaves open whether each constituent survives as it was.
boyle_lynx: Wild cat proverbial for its extraordinary eyesight in the debate on perceptible particles.
boyle_quart: Liquid measure of one quarter of a gallon, used for comparing volumes.
boyle_penetration: Supposed occupation of the same region of space by different bodies, as distinct from juxtaposition.
boyle_quartation: Historical refining operation so named because the alloy contains roughly one part of gold to three of silver.
boyle_turpentine: The resinous substance discussed as a source of oily products, distinct from the distilled oil alone.
boyle_minium: Red lead, the particular historical lead material distinguished by its red colour.
boyle_sugar_lead: The historical name Saccharum Saturni for the sweet lead salt. The name describes its reported taste. It is not ordinary sugar.
boyle_concretion: The resulting unified material produced when constituents combine, in the terminology Carneades proposes.
boyle_chyle: The pale digestive fluid considered a material antecedent of blood in the medical physiology discussed.
boyle_whey: The watery fraction of milk, here named alongside butter in the discussion of cream.
boyle_saturn_lead: Lead under its chymical planetary name Saturn, including the practitioners’ claim about transmutation.
boyle_brittleness: Disposition of a solid such as a salt to fracture easily, distinguished from hardness.
boyle_formative: Able to confer a particular organization on matter, historically the plastic power attributed to a seed.
boyle_electuary: A medicinal confection whose ingredients are mixed with a sweet carrier. Boyle compares mixtures with different ingredients.
boyle_tincture: The colour-bearing material reportedly extracted from a metal. Its status as a principle is disputed.
boyle_reverberatory: A furnace in which the heat is directed back upon the material.
boyle_corrosive: Capable of eating away or dissolving material; here said of a liquid reagent.
boyle_urinal: A laboratory vessel of the glass shape historically used for examination of urine.
boyle_cotton: Soft plant fibre used as a stopper in the glass vessel.
boyle_venus_copper: Copper under its traditional planetary name Venus.
boyle_verdigris: Green copper material. The speaker calls his residue an odd kind of verdigris.
boyle_effluvium: A material outflow inferred from actions at a distance, including those of amber and jet.
boyle_electric: Capable of the amber-like attraction described by Boyle, before the modern theory of electricity.
boyle_filing: A shaving or particle mechanically filed from a metal.
boyle_quintessence: The supposed highly purified essence of wine or another material in the chymical tradition; not an ordinary numbered fifth of a quantity.
boyle_syrup: Concentrated sweet liquid used here as a carrier for a violet colour indicator.
boyle_infusion: Liquid charged with constituents by steeping a material in it. Distinct from a distillate.
boyle_effervescence: Visible or audible evolution of bubbles during mixing, distinguished from boiling by external heat.
boyle_crab_eyes: Historical materia medica name for the hard concretions of crayfish, used here as an absorbent alongside coral and pearls.
boyle_temper_steel: To bring steel to a selected hardness by heating and cooling, in Boyle’s broad historical usage.
boyle_aqua_vitae: The historical Latin name for distilled wine spirit; in Helmont’s qualification, freed from aqueous phlegm.
boyle_sal_circulatum: Paracelsian sal circulatum, said by Helmont to separate ingredients and then be recovered unchanged.
boyle_decompound: A material itself compounded from one or more already compound ingredients, distinguished from a primary mixture.
boyle_bezoardic: Historical class of preparations named for supposed bezoar-like powers; Boyle analyses their successive compositions.
boyle_antimonial_butter: Historical antimonial preparation called butter from its appearance, distinct from dairy butter.
boyle_nitre: Saltpetre in the chymical vocabulary. Its adjectival use also covers the nitrous quality Boyle attributes to certain juices. Distinct from the biblical washing mineral.
boyle_reduction: Recovery of a metallic product from a calx or powder. Names a process, not merely making a quantity smaller.
boyle_hartshorn: Antler as the material used by early chymists to obtain volatile salt and spirit.
boyle_lye_salt: Salt recovered by leaching ashes. Describes extraction and distinguishes the alkaline product from the acid taste of unburned tartar.
boyle_tyrocinium: Tyrocinium Chymicum, the work by Jean Béguin.
boyle_precipitate_v: To cause a material to separate or fall as a solid; historical usage includes the dry product from quicksilver.
boyle_clove: Dried aromatic flower bud, likened in shape to a nail.
boyle_alum: The astringent salt named among the shop materials, distinguished from saltpetre.
boyle_eyebright: Flowering herb formerly prescribed for weak sight.
boyle_tobacco: Tobacco plant, whose stalks are burned here for salt.
boyle_parallelepiped: Solid bounded by three pairs of parallel plane faces.
boyle_rhombus: Equal-sided parallelogram, here the apparent outline of crystals.
boyle_nutmeg: Aromatic seed as distinct from the cloves and cinnamon in the comparisons.
boyle_lye: Alkaline liquor leached from ashes, distinguished from its crystallised salts.
boyle_evaporate: Cause liquid to pass off as vapour.
boyle_sediment: Matter settled to the bottom of a liquid.
boyle_clot: Pass from a liquid to a coherent or thicker body; a historical description of physical change.
boyle_lac: Insect-derived resin formerly designated gum lac, distinguished from tree resins.
boyle_benzoin: Aromatic tree resin, historically benjamin or benzoin.
boyle_jalap: Resin-bearing purgative root named in accounts of plant extracts.
boyle_pewter: Tin-based metal alloy, including the material of early modern pewter ware.
boyle_yolk: Yellow nutritive material of an egg, contrasted with the white.
boyle_tendon: Sinew attaching muscle to bone, distinguished from the nerve and blood vessels in the anatomical list.
boyle_axiom: First proposition accepted as the basis of an argument.
boyle_prism: Faceted glass whose cross section has three sides in this experiment.
boyle_gumarabic: Water-soluble gum from acacias, distinguished here from wine-spirit-soluble resins.
boyle_archaeus: The formative internal artificer in the cited account of underground production.
boyle_bladder: Organ holding urine, a site of urinary calculi.
boyle_spar: Crystalline stony gangue in which metal is found, without assigning it to a modern mineral species.
boyle_privation: In the Aristotelian account of change, absence of a form before the thing takes that form.
boyle_lapis_lazuli: Deep-blue mineral stone in the Helmont quotation.
boyle_loth: German weight called loth, twelve of which are equated here with six ounces.
boyle_flux: An additive used to promote fusion in assaying an ore or residue.
boyle_rennet: A substance used to coagulate milk and separate curd from whey.
boyle_verjuice: Sharp juice pressed from unripe grapes.
boyle_must: Freshly pressed grape juice before completion of fermentation.
boyle_marc: Pressed grape skins and solid residue after the juice has been expressed, called marc in French.
boyle_autopsia: Greek autopsia in the conclusion: seeing an experiment for oneself; firsthand inspection as a warrant for belief.
boyle_potential_fire: Historical term for an agent possessing the effective or dissolving power ascribed to fire, contrasted with actual fire.
